title: Which particle makes it nitrogen?
hook: Every atom is protons, neutrons and electrons. Add one to carbon. Which one renames it?

knows: that atoms contain protons, neutrons and electrons
the names carbon, nitrogen and oxygen
doesNotKnow: that only the proton count decides which element an atom is
that extra neutrons make a heavier version of the same element and extra electrons make it charged

misconception: Adding any particle, or more electrons, changes which element an atom is.
objective: The learner can say that a carbon atom (6 protons) becomes nitrogen only when a 7th proton is added; an extra neutron gives carbon-13 and an extra electron gives a charged carbon ion.

claims.text: The number of protons in an atom's nucleus (its atomic number) decides which element it is.
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book, 'atomic number' and 'chemical element' (a species of atoms all with the same number of protons).

claims.text: Carbon has 6 protons, nitrogen 7 and oxygen 8.
claims.source: IUPAC periodic table: C Z = 6, N Z = 7, O Z = 8. Demo.tsx ELEMENTS table.

claims.text: A carbon atom with 6 protons and 6 neutrons is carbon-12; one more neutron makes carbon-13, heavier but still carbon. The number after the name is protons plus neutrons.
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book, 'mass number' (A = Z + N) and 'isotopes'. C-12 and C-13 are both stable isotopes of carbon (NIST isotopic compositions). Demo.tsx computes mass = p + n.

claims.text: An extra electron leaves the element unchanged but gives the atom a charge of −1, making it an ion.
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book, 'ion'. Demo.tsx charge = protons − electrons.

claims.text: Adding a proton to a nucleus is a nuclear change, made in stars and particle accelerators, not by ordinary chemistry.
claims.source: Nuclear reactions change Z (e.g. proton capture in stellar nucleosynthesis, C-12 + p -> N-13; Krane, Introductory Nuclear Physics, ch. 11 and 19). Chemical reactions change only electrons.

claims.text: The picture is not to scale: the nucleus is about 100,000 times smaller across than the atom, and electrons are not dots on rings.
claims.source: Nuclear radius about 1e-15 m vs atomic radius about 1e-10 m (Krane, ch. 3). The ring picture is the Bohr-style cartoon; the stage labels it 'not to scale'.

recall.question: An atom has 8 protons, 9 neutrons and 10 electrons. Which element is it?
recall.why: The proton count names the element: 8 protons is oxygen. The extra neutron makes it heavier and the extra electrons make it charged, but it is still oxygen.
